shortAnswer: If Amazon KDP says your cover size does not match your interior, your cover PDF was probably built for different book settings than the interior you uploaded. Check trim size, final page count, paper type, bleed, and spine width, then rebuild the full wraparound cover to match those exact settings.

faqs.question: Why does KDP say my cover size does not match interior?
faqs.answer: KDP shows this warning when the uploaded cover PDF dimensions do not match the book setup implied by your interior: trim size, page count, paper type, bleed, and spine width. The cover may be too wide, too narrow, too tall, or built for a different version of the book.

faqs.question: Does changing page count affect KDP cover size?
faqs.answer: Yes. For paperback and hardcover print books, page count changes spine width. When the spine width changes, the total full cover width changes too, even if the front cover trim size stays the same.

faqs.question: Can I upload only a front cover to KDP paperback?
faqs.answer: No. For a KDP paperback print book, the cover file should be a full wraparound PDF that includes back cover, spine, front cover, and bleed where required.

faqs.question: Why did my cover work before but fail after I changed the interior?
faqs.answer: The interior change probably altered page count, bleed expectations, or trim setup. If the cover was designed from the old interior settings, KDP now compares it against a different book specification.

faqs.question: Does bleed affect KDP cover dimensions?
faqs.answer: Yes. A print cover with bleed is larger than the final trim size because the artwork extends beyond the trim edge. If bleed is missing, added twice, or exported with extra crop marks, the PDF dimensions can fail KDP checks.

faqs.question: How do I know the correct KDP cover size?
faqs.answer: Use the final trim size, final page count, selected paper type, ink type, binding type, and bleed setting. Then generate a fresh KDP cover template or use a reliable cover size calculator before exporting the cover PDF.

faqs.question: Can Canva cause KDP cover size mismatch errors?
faqs.answer: Yes. Common Canva mistakes include designing only the front cover size, entering custom dimensions incorrectly, exporting with extra white borders, or using a canvas that does not include the spine and back cover.

faqs.question: Should I design my KDP cover before or after the interior?
faqs.answer: Design the final cover after the interior is final, or be prepared to recalculate the cover every time page count, trim size, paper type, or bleed settings change.

content:
If Amazon KDP says your cover size does not match your interior, it usually means the cover PDF was built for different book settings than the interior you uploaded. The design may look fine on screen, but KDP is checking the technical size of the PDF against the trim size, page count, paper type, bleed settings, and spine width in your book setup.

This is a fixable production problem. It does not mean your cover art is bad, and it usually does not mean you need to start over. It means one part of the book package changed or was calculated from the wrong values.

The most important thing to understand is this: changing the interior file can change the required cover size. If you add pages, remove pages, switch paper type, change trim size, or export the interior with different bleed settings, the cover may no longer match. KDP compares the cover against the current book settings, not the settings you used when you first designed the file.

## What Does "Cover Size Does Not Match Interior" Mean?

When KDP says the cover size does not match interior, it is comparing your uploaded cover PDF with the print book setup it expects from your interior and product settings. For a paperback or hardcover, the cover is not just a front image. It is a full production file.

For paperback covers, KDP expects a single PDF that includes the back cover, spine, front cover, and bleed if needed. The front and back panels must match the trim size selected in KDP. The spine must match the page count and paper type. The height must match the trim height plus bleed if the cover uses bleed.

If one of those values is off, KDP may reject the cover, warn that the preview is inaccurate, or show a size mismatch message. Sometimes the file is only slightly wrong. Sometimes the cover was built for a completely different trim size. Either way, KDP is telling you that the physical cover wrap does not match the book block created by the interior.

Think of the interior as the stack of printed pages. The cover has to wrap around that stack. If the stack becomes thicker, thinner, taller, shorter, or uses a different trim size, the cover wrap has to change too.

## Why This Error Happens

The KDP cover size error usually comes from one of these setup mismatches.

### Wrong Trim Size Selected in KDP

Your trim size is the final cut size of the book, such as 6 x 9 inches, 5.5 x 8.5 inches, or 8.5 x 11 inches. If your interior was made for 6 x 9 but your KDP setup says 5.5 x 8.5, KDP will expect a different cover size. The front and back panels of the cover will not line up with the interior.

This can happen when authors test different book sizes and forget to update the cover file after changing the setup.

### Cover Designed for a Different Trim Size

You may have selected the right trim size in KDP, but the cover itself may have been designed for another size. A cover built for 6 x 9 cannot simply be uploaded to an 8.5 x 11 book. The proportions, height, width, spine position, safe area, and bleed all change.

If you reused a previous book cover template, check the template dimensions before exporting again.

### Page Count Changed After the Cover Was Designed

This is the most common cause. Paperback cover width depends on spine width, and spine width depends on page count. If the manuscript was 120 pages when the cover was designed but is 140 pages now, the spine is different.

KDP does not resize your spine automatically. The cover PDF has to be rebuilt or adjusted to the new full wrap width.

### Paper Type Changed After the Cover Was Designed

Paper type affects spine thickness. White paper, cream paper, and color interior paper can have different thickness constants. A 200-page book on one paper type may require a slightly different spine than the same page count on another paper type.

This is why you should confirm paper type before generating your final cover template.

### Bleed or No-Bleed Mismatch

Bleed is extra artwork that extends beyond the trim edge so the printed book can be cut cleanly. If your cover has edge-to-edge artwork, it usually needs bleed. If the cover PDF was exported without bleed, the dimensions may be too small. If crop marks or extra margins were added, the dimensions may be too large.

Bleed mistakes often create height and width mismatches that are easy to miss in Canva, Photoshop, or Affinity.

### Incorrect Spine Width

The spine sits between the back cover and front cover. If it is too narrow, the full cover PDF may be too narrow. If it is too wide, the cover may not wrap correctly around the book block.

Spine width mismatch is especially common when authors update the interior but keep uploading the same cover draft.

### Canva Custom Size Entered Incorrectly

Canva can work for KDP covers, but the custom size must be the full cover size, not only the front cover size. A common mistake is creating an 8.5 x 11 design for a book with an 8.5 x 11 trim, then uploading it as a paperback cover. That is only the front panel. A print cover needs back cover + spine + front cover + bleed.

### Photoshop Canvas Size Set Incorrectly

Photoshop gives you full control, which also means it will not protect you from wrong dimensions. If the canvas is set to the front cover size only, or if the spine width is missing, the exported PDF will not match KDP expectations.

### Using an Old KDP Template

KDP templates are generated from specific book settings. If you download a template, then later change page count, trim size, paper type, or binding type, the old template may no longer be valid.

Use a fresh template after the interior is final.

### Exporting With Crop Marks or Extra Margins

Some PDF export settings add crop marks, printer marks, white margins, or extra page boxes. KDP reads the actual PDF dimensions. If the export adds space around your cover, the file may become larger than expected even though the artwork itself looks right.

### Uploading the Wrong Version of the File

This sounds simple, but it happens constantly. Authors fix the cover, export a corrected file, then accidentally upload the older draft from Downloads or a previous project folder. If the warning makes no sense, check the filename, timestamp, and PDF dimensions.

## The Most Common Cause: Page Count Changed

A 120-page book and a 140-page book with the same trim size do not use the same full cover width.

The front cover panel may still be 6 x 9 inches, but the spine is not the same. More pages make the spine wider. Fewer pages make it narrower. The total cover width changes because the spine sits between the back and front panels.

This is why the error often appears after small interior edits. You may add a copyright page, remove blank pages, change margins, change font size, add images, or export the manuscript again. Even if the trim size stays the same, the final page count can move enough to change the required cover wrap.

Blank pages matter too. If you add blank pages to force chapters to start on the right side, those pages still count. If you remove blank pages at the end of the manuscript, those pages disappear from the spine calculation.

Interiors with bleed can also affect setup expectations because KDP is checking the uploaded interior dimensions and production settings together. If the interior and product setup do not agree, the cover comparison can become confusing.

The safest workflow is to finalize the interior first, then calculate the cover from the final page count. If you must design the cover early, treat it as a draft until the interior is locked.

## How KDP Calculates Paperback Cover Size

You do not need to memorize complicated math, but you should understand the basic relationship.

Full cover width = back cover + spine width + front cover + bleed.

Full cover height = trim height + top bleed + bottom bleed.

For a paperback, the front cover and back cover are each based on the trim size. The spine width is calculated from the book block. Bleed adds extra area around the outside edges when the design reaches the edge.

Spine width depends on:

- page count
- ink type
- paper type
- binding type
- marketplace or template settings

That is why guessing is risky. A cover that is close can still fail. Use updated KDP template dimensions or a reliable [KDP trim size calculator](/tools/kdp-trim-size-calculator) and [spine width calculator](/tools/kdp-spine-width-calculator) before exporting the final PDF.

## Step-by-Step Fix Workflow

### Step 1: Check the Trim Size Selected in KDP

Open your KDP paperback or hardcover setup and confirm the trim size. Do not rely on memory. Check the exact size selected in the print options.

Then compare it with the size used in your interior file and cover design. If the KDP setup says 6 x 9 but your files were built for 5.5 x 8.5, choose the correct trim size or rebuild the files.

### Step 2: Check the Interior Page Count

Look at the final page count of the uploaded interior. Use the final exported PDF, not the page count in your writing software. Word, Google Docs, Vellum, Atticus, InDesign, and PDF readers can show different values if front matter, blank pages, or export settings changed.

If the page count changed after the cover was designed, recalculate the cover width.

### Step 3: Confirm Paper Type and Ink Type

Check whether the book uses black and white interior, standard color, premium color, white paper, or cream paper. These choices can affect spine width and template expectations.

If you changed paper type after downloading a KDP template, generate a new template.

### Step 4: Regenerate or Recalculate the Cover Size

Use the current trim size, final page count, paper type, ink type, binding type, and bleed setting. Generate a fresh KDP cover template or calculate the cover dimensions again.

Do not reuse old cover dimensions unless every book setting is identical.

### Step 5: Compare the PDF Dimensions

Open the exported cover PDF and check its page size. Compare the PDF width and height with the expected full cover dimensions.

If the PDF is too narrow, the spine or bleed may be missing. If it is too wide, the spine may be calculated from an old page count or the export may include extra marks or margins.

### Step 6: Fix the Canvas Size in Canva, Photoshop, or Affinity

Update the design file canvas to the full cover size. Make sure the cover includes back cover, spine, front cover, and bleed if needed.

Do not resize only the artwork. The actual document or canvas size must match the required PDF size.

### Step 7: Re-Export as a Print-Ready PDF

Export a clean print PDF. Avoid extra white borders, printer marks, or accidental scaling. Embed fonts where the tool allows it and keep image quality high.

After export, check the PDF dimensions again. The exported file is what KDP reads, not the design canvas.

### Step 8: Upload Again and Check Previewer

Upload the corrected cover PDF to KDP. Open Previewer and inspect the trim, spine, and back cover. If KDP still warns about size, return to the PDF dimensions and compare them with the current setup.

Before uploading again, run your cover through [KDPPreflight](/tools/kdp-cover-checker) to check whether the full cover size, bleed, trim, and spine area are aligned with your book setup.

## Canva Fix Workflow

Canva is often where KDP cover size mismatch errors begin because authors start with the visible front cover size instead of the full print cover size.

For a paperback cover, your Canva custom size must match the full cover dimensions. That means back cover + spine + front cover + bleed. If your book trim is 8.5 x 11, do not create only an 8.5 x 11 Canva document and upload it as the print cover. That is only one panel.

Start by calculating the full cover size from your current KDP setup. Then create or resize the Canva design to those exact dimensions in inches. If Canva asks for width and height, the width should be the full wrap width, not the front cover width.

Do not add random white margins around the design. KDP does not want a screenshot-like page with blank space around the cover. It wants the actual cover PDF at the production size.

If your artwork reaches the edge, extend the background to the bleed area. The bleed is for background art, colors, and images. Keep important text, logos, subtitles, and author names away from the trim edge and inside the [safe area](/glossary/safe-area).

When exporting, use PDF Print. Avoid crop marks unless you intentionally need them and know they will not change the final page size. Many KDP cover workflows do not need crop marks from Canva; they need correct PDF dimensions.

After export, check the final PDF size if possible. If the exported PDF page size does not match the calculated full cover size, fix the Canva document before uploading again.

## Photoshop Fix Workflow

Photoshop is a good tool for precise KDP covers, but only if the canvas is set correctly.

Create the file in inches, not pixels first. Use the full cover width and full cover height from your current KDP setup. Set resolution to 300 DPI for print-quality artwork. The resolution affects pixel density, but the canvas dimensions in inches must still match the cover size.

The canvas should include the full wraparound cover: back cover, spine, front cover, and bleed. Do not create only the front panel unless you are making an ebook cover or a separate marketing image.

Add guides for:

- outer bleed edge
- trim line
- safe area
- back cover panel
- spine panel
- front cover panel
- barcode clearance area

Guides help you see where the spine begins and where important content should stay. They do not change the PDF size by themselves, so the canvas still has to be correct.

When exporting, avoid settings that add unexpected margins or scale the artwork to fit a different page. Export a high-quality PDF and verify the dimensions after export. If the PDF dimensions changed, the export settings need attention before KDP will accept the file.

## How to Check If Your Cover PDF Size Is Correct

The fastest way to diagnose an Amazon KDP cover size mismatch is to check the PDF page size.

Open the cover PDF in a PDF reader or design tool that can show document properties. Look for the page size in inches. Compare that width and height with the dimensions from your current KDP template or calculator.

If KDP says the cover file does not match the interior, check these values:

- Is the PDF width the full cover width?
- Is the PDF height the expected cover height?
- Does the width include the spine?
- Does the width include bleed when required?
- Does the height include top and bottom bleed when required?
- Was the spine calculated from the final interior page count?

You can also upload the file to KDP Previewer, but Previewer is not always the easiest place to diagnose the cause. It may tell you there is a mismatch without clearly showing whether trim size, spine, bleed, or export dimensions caused it.

Before uploading again, run your cover through [KDPPreflight](/tools/kdp-cover-checker) to check whether the full cover size, bleed, trim, and spine area are aligned with your book setup.

## Common Mistakes That Trigger This Error

### Using Front Cover Dimensions Only

A paperback cover is not a front cover image. It is a full wrap PDF. If you upload only the front cover dimensions, the file will be too narrow because it is missing the back cover and spine.

### Changing Page Count After Designing the Cover

Every page count change can affect spine width. If the interior changed after the cover was built, recalculate the cover.

### Using the Wrong Paper Type

Paper thickness affects spine width. A cover designed for one paper type may not match another paper type.

### Using No-Bleed Dimensions for a Bleed Cover

If your cover has artwork to the edge but the PDF was exported at trim-only dimensions, KDP may see the cover as too small.

### Exporting From Canva With an Extra White Border

Extra white borders can make the PDF larger than expected or create artwork that does not reach bleed. Use the correct custom size instead of adding margin manually.

### Forgetting the Spine

If the spine is missing, the cover cannot wrap around the book. Even a blank spine still takes up physical width.

### Using a Template for Another Trim Size

A template for 5 x 8 will not work for 6 x 9. A template for 120 pages will not always work for 140 pages.

### Uploading an Older Draft

If you fixed everything and the error remains, make sure the file you uploaded is the corrected export. Check the filename and modified date.

## How to Prevent This Error Before Uploading

The best prevention is to stop treating the cover as separate from the interior. For print books, they are connected.

Finalize the interior first. Confirm the trim size. Export the interior and check the final page count. Confirm paper type, ink type, bleed, and binding. Then generate a fresh cover template or calculate the full wraparound cover size.

Build the cover at the full wraparound size from the beginning. Keep text inside safe areas. Keep background artwork extended into bleed. Recheck PDF dimensions after export.

Finally, run a preflight check before KDP upload. A preflight pass can catch trim, bleed, spine, and PDF-size problems while you are still in control, instead of after KDP rejects the file.

## Quick Checklist Before Reuploading to KDP

- Trim size matches interior
- Page count is final
- Paper type is correct
- Cover includes front, back, spine
- Spine width matches page count
- Bleed included if needed
- PDF exported without extra margins
- Background extends to bleed
- Text stays inside safe area
- File uploaded is the latest version

## FAQ

### Why does KDP say my cover size does not match interior?

KDP says this when the cover PDF dimensions do not match the book setup implied by your interior file. The mismatch may come from trim size, page count, paper type, bleed, spine width, or export dimensions.

### Does changing page count affect KDP cover size?

Yes. Page count changes spine width. Since the spine is part of the full cover width, changing page count can make the old cover too narrow or too wide.

### Can I upload only a front cover to KDP paperback?

No. For a KDP paperback, upload a full wraparound cover PDF with back cover, spine, front cover, and bleed if needed. A front-cover-only image is not enough for print.

### Why did my cover work before but fail after I changed the interior?

The interior change probably changed the page count, trim setup, or bleed expectations. KDP is now checking the cover against the newer interior settings.

### Does bleed affect KDP cover dimensions?

Yes. Bleed adds extra area beyond the trim edge. If bleed is missing, added incorrectly, or exported with extra marks, the cover dimensions may not match KDP expectations.

### How do I know the correct KDP cover size?

Use your final trim size, final page count, paper type, ink type, binding type, and bleed setting. Generate a fresh KDP template or use a reliable [KDP cover calculator](/tools/kdp-trim-size-calculator).

### Can Canva cause KDP cover size mismatch errors?

Yes. Canva can cause errors when the document is only the front cover size, when custom dimensions are entered incorrectly, or when the PDF export adds borders or misses bleed.

### Should I design my KDP cover before or after the interior?

Design the final print cover after the interior is final. If you design earlier, expect to update the cover after every page count or setup change.

## Final Check Before You Upload Again

The fix is usually straightforward: make the cover match the book that KDP is actually printing. Confirm the trim size, use the final page count, recalculate the spine, include bleed if needed, and export a clean full wraparound PDF.

If you are not sure whether your cover size matches your interior, upload your file to [KDPPreflight](/tools/kdp-cover-checker) before submitting it to Amazon KDP. It is easier to catch trim, bleed, spine, and safe-area problems before KDP rejects the file.
